material_findings.reasoning: The sequence extract/scan/rescan/release does not define what happens to ZIP members that cannot be decrypted or are excluded by scan limits. A nested password-protected member can remain as archive content after outer extraction. The selected supported source has a known unscanned path, and the default alerts need not distinguish it from absence of a malware detection. The generic warning that not detected does not mean clean acknowledges signature coverage but supplies no gate/report policy for known unscanned inputs. Repeating the same scan after definition updates does not resolve an unknown password or unchanged size limit. None of the seven proposed validations checks this distinction; there is also no positive scanner routing or error/partial-scan witness in the final matrix. This is a basic accepted-input condition, not a demand for perfect antivirus detection or unlimited guarantees. No runtime result was falsely claimed.

### MF4 — Encrypted ZIP members can pass the malware gate unscanned; absent from mechanisms and test matrix
P1 accepts ZIP uploads and P3 gates on a ClamAV scan (research/draft.md;
research/sources/S02). ClamAV cannot decrypt password-protected archive members; the
documented behavior is an *alert on the fact of encryption*, and it is off by default:
clamd.conf(5) documents `AlertEncrypted` ("Alert on encrypted archives and documents
(encrypted .zip, .7zip, .rar, .pdf)"), `AlertEncryptedArchive` ("Alert on encrypted archives
(encrypted .zip, .7zip, .rar)"), and `AlertEncryptedDoc`, each **"Default: no"** (C09,
https://manpages.debian.org/trixie/clamav-daemon/clamd.conf.5.en.html; the same options and
defaults appear in the upstream clamd.conf.sample in the Cisco-Talos/clamav repository, seen
in search excerpts; the attempted direct raw fetch 404'd at the guessed path). A donor can
therefore place arbitrary content in an encrypted member and the out-of-the-box scanner sees
nothing inside — while the draft's P6 matrix tests EICAR only in a plain package and P1's
correction names path traversal (zip-slip) and size limits but never encryption. This
directly attacks the brief's core "malware/quarantine separation" need. Required design
response (proposed, not executed): an explicit service policy — reject encrypted archives, or
enable encrypted-archive alerting and route to the failed path — plus a discriminating
validation: an encrypted ZIP containing the EICAR test string must never be reported clean.
Related, same origin, lower confidence: ClamAV cannot scan a ZIP from a non-seekable stream
(search-corroborated via exav.org; secondary-only) — relevant only if the service ever pipes
archives to the scanner. Evidence: research/draft.md P1/P6; research/sources/S02; C09.
Uncertainty: the man page documents the alert options and their defaults; that member
contents are skipped is the documented reason these alerts exist, but no single fetched
sentence states it verbatim — flagged rather than overquoted.

criticism_adjudication.independent_reasoning: Correct RFC location is §2.2.3. The transport mechanism is real. A section-number error is not the substantive material pointer-fetch gap.
An informal bagit.zip-style label is not a normative profile. Packaging a compliant bag in a ZIP remains viable; this is naming/interchange-profile precision rather than evidence against P1.

CVE-2021-22204 is ExifTool DjVu; CVE-2021-36370 is Midnight Commander. The discovery explicitly withheld the latter mapping as unverified. Do not turn a stated uncertainty into an authored wrong fact.

Unknown-password content and disabled alerts can undermine the proposed gate; that is material. ClamAV does try password databases, so a categorical cannot-decrypt claim is too broad. Scope to members actually unscanned and test/report that state.

A chosen pointer-fetcher needs trust/resource policy. bagit-python 1.9 validates URI syntax and destination paths; it does not fetch URLs. #154 does not prove validator local-file/network reads or an exploit. Conditional fetcher risk is distinct from library behavior.

A dated latest release alone neither proves inactivity nor proves active maintenance. The repository and 2025 release support a real candidate tool; do not infer a material maintenance conclusion from elapsed months.
Production and newest listed ExifTool versions are different official labels.
#154 concerns file-URL validation syntax, not a new fetch implementation. This undercuts MF5’s stronger factual inference.
Old quarantine documentation and a custom rescan-on-release proposal need distinct applicability. Configurable policy is permitted; no universal waiting-period claim is required.
Whether P1 is called corrected, enhanced or kept-with-conditions is partly presentation. The actual constraint remains ZIP support with validation and a donor choice; do not fail solely on the label.
P5’s original-name intent is retained with safer storage keys and mappings. Adding an already-covered label may help, but absence of that exact label is not a defect.

Legacy algorithms and ordinary oversize cases are useful tests, not an exhaustive mandatory production suite. Scan coverage limits are consequential to the selected release gate and are covered by S01.
The six dispositions have each been assessed below; critic endorsement was not used as an oracle. P4 embedded repair is an optional route rather than a requirement to abandon post-import staff edits.
Preserve useful report taxonomy, pointer-fetch and scanner conditions, while qualifying the asserted decryption and fetch behavior. No mandatory unrelated workflow was inferred.

Plain EICAR, malformed bags, deliberate digest substitution and a defined DjVu fixture can be discriminating. The critic incorrectly approves the parser-CVE test’s expected detection misses. Release-specific vulnerability behavior is a different oracle.

The brief does not require actually running all proposals, a particular NVD page, a universal quarantine duration, real paid infrastructure or citations for every design preference. Available primary evidence is still required for consequential selected-tool behavior.

The DjVu CVE mapping is resolved by vendor/Debian evidence; exposure of metadata writing versus the vulnerable reader is not separately established. Donor familiarity and actual version-difference runtimes remain untested. Current built-in quarantine applicability is resolved by removal in1.11. Upstream unzip code now independently confirms the unknown-password skip, with password-database exceptions. The non-seekable-stream aside remains secondary and is not a selected implemented transport claim. Source lists and retrieval timestamps are lineage, not executed security witnesses or independent provider/native chronology.

proposed_validations.independent_oracle_and_applicability: Plain EICAR can distinguish positive detection and failed routing from a wait-only state when the selected engine recognizes it. It does not prove unknown-password or partial-scan disposition. No actual run was claimed.

A custom hold with updated definitions can reveal whether a second scan happens, using event/scan assertions. A clean sample alone may give identical outcomes; assert invocation and definition versions, not just final acceptance. Current Archivematica has no old built-in quarantine feature.
Missing/corrupt bags distinguish complete versus valid failure classes. Donor comprehension is an appropriate proposed report evaluation, not a demonstrated result.
Chosen file-URI and unsafe-path fixtures can expose 1.8.1/1.9.0 differences. Running syntax validation does not validate a separate fetcher or prove local/network reads.
Wrong detection-miss oracle for parser RCE/information-disclosure CVEs and invalid current-supported ≥1.0.1 predicate. S03 grounds this material proposal defect.

Changing payload and its matching digest can leave a syntactically complete valid bag. This meaningfully demonstrates why fixity is not provenance, subject to updating every relevant manifest. No authenticating signature is assumed.

A specifically known DjVu vulnerability fixture and version/backport comparison could test the ExifTool parser fix. Arbitrary malformed DjVu may not discriminate. Upstream12.24 is the historical fix; distro backports matter. This remains a proposed sandbox experiment.
